animals.habitat: Forests, meadows, agricultural areas, suburban edges
animals.blurb: The most widespread deer in North America, recognized by the white underside of its tail which flashes when alarmed. Males grow and shed antlers annually. They are crepuscular, most active at dawn and dusk.
animals.hint: Look for a graceful browser with a distinctive white flag tail

animals.habitat: Deciduous and mixed forests, urban parks, suburban yards
animals.blurb: A highly adaptable tree squirrel known for its bushy tail and acrobatic abilities. They cache thousands of nuts each fall, inadvertently planting trees when they forget burial locations.
animals.hint: A bushy-tailed acrobat often seen in parks and backyards

animals.habitat: Forests, marshes, urban areas, anywhere near water
animals.blurb: Instantly recognizable by their black mask and ringed tail, raccoons are highly intelligent and dexterous. Their sensitive front paws can manipulate objects with remarkable precision.
animals.hint: A masked bandit with nimble paws and a ringed tail

animals.habitat: Forests, grasslands, mountains, farms, suburban areas
animals.blurb: The most widely distributed wild carnivore on Earth, famous for its rusty red coat and bushy white-tipped tail. They are solitary hunters with exceptional hearing that can locate prey under snow.
animals.hint: A rusty-coated canine with a white-tipped bushy tail

animals.blurb: North America's only marsupial, famous for 'playing possum' when threatened. They have prehensile tails and are remarkably resistant to rabies and venomous snake bites.
animals.hint: North America's only marsupial with a naked tail

animals.blurb: Famous for their powerful defensive spray that can be detected up to a mile away. Their bold black and white coloration serves as a warning to predators to keep their distance.
animals.hint: A bold black and white animal with a famous defensive spray

animals.blurb: Nature's premier engineers, beavers build dams that create entire ecosystems. Their flat, paddle-shaped tails are used for swimming, balance, and alarm signals.
animals.hint: A large rodent engineer with a flat, paddle-shaped tail

animals.blurb: Also known as woodchucks, these large ground squirrels are true hibernators. They excavate extensive burrow systems and are famous for their role in Groundhog Day predictions.
animals.hint: A chunky ground squirrel famous for shadow-watching

animals.habitat: Meadows, fields, forest edges, suburban areas
animals.blurb: The most common rabbit in North America, named for its powder-puff white tail. They can run up to 18 mph in a zigzag pattern to escape predators.
animals.hint: A common rabbit with a puffy white tail

animals.blurb: The most common and widely distributed bear in North America. Despite their name, they can be brown, cinnamon, or blonde. Excellent climbers, they spend much of their time foraging for berries and nuts.
animals.hint: A forest-dwelling bear that's an excellent climber

animals.blurb: A powerful subspecies of brown bear with a distinctive shoulder hump and grizzled fur. They can weigh over 800 pounds and are important seed dispersers and salmon nutrient transporters.
animals.hint: A massive bear with a shoulder hump and grizzled fur

animals.blurb: The largest wild member of the dog family, gray wolves live in complex social packs. Their howls can be heard up to 10 miles away and serve to communicate with pack members.
animals.hint: A social pack hunter with a haunting howl

animals.blurb: One of the most adaptable mammals in North America, coyotes have expanded their range despite human persecution. Their yipping howls are iconic sounds of the American wilderness.
animals.hint: An adaptable wild canine with a yipping howl

animals.blurb: The most common wild cat in North America, named for its short 'bobbed' tail. They are stealthy ambush predators with excellent night vision and hearing.
animals.hint: A wild cat with tufted ears and a short bobbed tail

animals.blurb: Also called cougar or puma, this is the largest wild cat in North America. Solitary and elusive, they can leap 40 feet horizontally and are powerful enough to take down elk.
animals.hint: A large, tawny cat that stalks mountain terrain

animals.blurb: The largest member of the deer family, bulls can weigh up to 1,500 pounds with antlers spanning 6 feet. Despite their size, they are excellent swimmers and can dive underwater to feed.
animals.hint: The largest deer with massive palmate antlers

animals.blurb: One of the largest deer species, famous for the bugling calls bulls make during the fall rut. Their impressive antlers can weigh up to 40 pounds.
animals.hint: A large deer known for bugling calls in autumn

animals.blurb: Named for their large, mule-like ears, these deer bound away using a distinctive stiff-legged hop called stotting. Their forked antlers distinguish them from white-tails.
animals.hint: A western deer with large ears and forked antlers

animals.blurb: The fastest land animal in the Western Hemisphere, capable of running 55 mph. Often mistakenly called antelope, they are uniquely American with no close living relatives.
animals.hint: North America's speedster with distinctive face markings

animals.blurb: The largest land mammal in North America, once numbering 30-60 million before near-extinction. Conservation efforts have brought them back from fewer than 1,000 animals.
animals.hint: A massive, hump-shouldered grazer of the plains

animals.blurb: Playful and social, river otters spend much of their time sliding down muddy banks and wrestling with family members. Their webbed feet and waterproof fur make them expert swimmers.
animals.hint: A playful, sleek swimmer that loves to slide

animals.blurb: A semi-aquatic predator with luxurious dark fur. They are fierce hunters that can take prey larger than themselves, including muskrats and rabbits.
animals.hint: A sleek, dark-furred predator of waterways

animals.blurb: Despite their name, fishers rarely eat fish. They are one of the few predators skilled enough to hunt porcupines, attacking their face to avoid the quills.
animals.hint: A forest-dwelling weasel that hunts porcupines

animals.blurb: A powerful digger with strong front claws, badgers can excavate faster than a human with a shovel. They sometimes hunt cooperatively with coyotes.
animals.hint: A flat, wide-bodied digger with distinctive face stripes

animals.blurb: A slender, agile hunter that can pursue prey into burrows. In northern regions, they turn white in winter except for their black-tipped tail.
animals.hint: A slender hunter that may turn white in winter

animals.blurb: The second-largest rodent in North America, covered in about 30,000 barbed quills. Contrary to myth, they cannot shoot their quills but release them on contact.
animals.hint: A slow-moving rodent armed with thousands of quills

animals.blurb: A semi-aquatic rodent that builds dome-shaped lodges similar to beavers. Their name comes from the musky odor they produce to mark territory.
animals.hint: A wetland rodent with a naked, scaly tail

animals.blurb: Another name for the groundhog, this large ground squirrel is a true hibernator whose body temperature drops to near freezing during winter dormancy.
animals.hint: How much wood would this ground squirrel chuck?

animals.blurb: The largest tree squirrel in North America, with highly variable coloration from silver-gray to black. They spend more time on the ground than gray squirrels.
animals.hint: The largest tree squirrel with variable coloration

animals.blurb: A small, territorial squirrel known for its loud, chattering alarm calls. They create large middens of pine cone scales that can accumulate over many generations.
animals.hint: A small, noisy squirrel that scolds intruders

animals.blurb: A small, striped ground squirrel with expandable cheek pouches that can hold up to 32 beechnuts at once. They spend winter in underground burrows.
animals.hint: A tiny striped squirrel with bulging cheek pouches

animals.blurb: One of the most common bats in North America, a single bat can eat up to 1,000 mosquitoes per hour. White-nose syndrome has devastated their populations.
animals.hint: A small flying mammal that devours mosquitoes

animals.blurb: A robust bat commonly found in buildings and bridges. They are important pest controllers, consuming large quantities of beetles and other agricultural pests.
animals.hint: A common bat often roosting in buildings

animals.blurb: The only armadillo found in the United States, expanding northward rapidly. They always give birth to identical quadruplets and can hold their breath for up to 6 minutes.
animals.hint: An armored mammal with a bony shell

animals.blurb: An invasive species that causes billions of dollars in damage annually. They are intelligent, adaptable, and reproduce rapidly, making them difficult to control.
animals.hint: A tusked invasive pig causing ecological damage

animals.blurb: The largest land carnivore, polar bears are actually classified as marine mammals. Their white fur is actually transparent, and their skin underneath is black.
animals.hint: The white giant of the Arctic ice

animals.blurb: The smallest marine mammal, sea otters have the densest fur of any animal—up to a million hairs per square inch. They use rocks as tools to crack open shellfish.
animals.hint: A floating fur-ball that uses rocks as tools

animals.blurb: Despite their name, mountain goats are not true goats but are more closely related to antelopes. Their rubbery hoof pads provide excellent grip on steep terrain.
animals.hint: A white climber scaling impossible cliffs

animals.habitat: Rocky mountains, alpine meadows, desert hills
animals.blurb: Males are famous for their spectacular head-butting battles during mating season, clashing with forces up to 800 pounds. Their curved horns can weigh 30 pounds.
animals.hint: A mountain dweller famous for dramatic head-butting

animals.habitat: Domestic environments, varied habitats alongside humans
animals.blurb: The domestic dog is humanity's oldest companion, descended from wolves and domesticated over 15,000 years ago. They display remarkable diversity in size, shape, and behavior across hundreds of breeds.
animals.hint: A loyal mammal often found in homes and parks

animals.habitat: Domestic environments, urban and rural areas
animals.blurb: The domestic cat is a small predator that has lived alongside humans for nearly 10,000 years. They retain strong hunting instincts and are crepuscular, most active at dawn and dusk.
animals.hint: An independent feline companion found worldwide

animals.blurb: Domesticated over 10,000 years ago from wild aurochs, cattle are among the most widespread large mammals on Earth. They are ruminants with a four-chambered stomach, allowing them to digest tough grasses. Cows are social animals that form strong bonds within their herds.
animals.hint: A large, gentle grazer commonly found on farms and pastures
